title: Binary Search: Interval Conventions, Boundary Updates, and Applicability
evidence_note: The supplied fixture (fixture_binary_search_en) explicitly covers closed and half-open interval conventions, midpoint computation, boundary updates, termination conditions, complexity, and applicability constraints, which is sufficient for one easy multiple-choice question.
learning_objectives: Explain how a closed search interval [left, right] represents the positions still eligible to hold the target.
Identify the correct boundary update and termination condition consistent with the closed-interval convention.

sections.heading: Closed interval and eligibility
sections.text: Binary search uses the ordering of a sequence to discard positions that cannot hold the target. In the closed convention, the search interval [left, right] contains every position still eligible to hold the target; initially left is zero and right is n minus one (fixture_binary_search_en).

sections.heading: Midpoint and boundary updates
sections.text: At each iteration, mid = left + floor((right - left) / 2). If the middle value is smaller than the target, all positions through mid are too small, so set left = mid + 1. If it is larger, positions from mid onward are too large, so set right = mid - 1 (fixture_binary_search_en).

sections.heading: Termination and absent target
sections.text: The loop runs while left <= right; an empty interval means the target is absent. The interval convention determines the termination condition, and mixing a closed-interval test with a half-open right boundary can inspect a position outside the array (fixture_binary_search_en).

questions.stem: Using the closed-interval convention [left, right] described in the notes, which statement correctly pairs the loop condition with the update applied when the middle value is larger than the target? (fixture_binary_search_en)
options: Loop while left <= right; set right = mid - 1
Loop while left < right; set right = mid
Loop while left <= right; set left = mid + 1
Loop while left < right; set right = mid - 1
questions.explanation: In the closed convention the interval [left, right] is nonempty while left <= right, and when the middle value is larger than the target, positions from mid onward are too large, so right = mid - 1 (fixture_binary_search_en).
questions.difficulty_reason: This is an easy item: it asks the student to recognize a single explicitly stated fact from the notes, with complete conditions and no strategy selection required.

expected_steps: Recall that the closed interval stays nonempty while left <= right.
Recall that a larger middle value sets right = mid - 1.

visual_prompt: A horizontal array of sorted cells with left and right markers showing the closed interval [left, right], a mid marker, and an arrow indicating that when the middle value is larger than the target, right moves to mid - 1.
